events: An unusual number of dead insects tend to be found on the windowsills of the characters' haven.
An old woman appears in a surprising place, like a nightclub bathroom, and tells a character she can see they are a good person.
Every fortune cookie the character sees for a week contains the same message: Ahoy bass no crying north Mrs Dash 1000 Kim.
A mound of fake fingernails appears on a grave the character visits.
A coyote and a corgi fight to the death in plain sight, but nobody seems to remark on it.
Letters burn out on the neon VACATION sign at the travel agent, spelling CA I N
One of the character's old prescription medicine bottles (with their name on the label) resurfaces in an alchemist's lab.
A human spontaneously combusts while watching Nosferatu at a revival house.
Three lights appear in the top of the old lighthouse, where the single lamp burned out decades ago.
A flock of pigeons begins to settle on the statue in the park but suddenly panics and explodes off it. It remains clear of birds for three days.
The sun sets with a green flash.
Right after the rain, the soot on the side of the factory building looks like a clawed hand print.
A character starts dreaming of dragonflies.

The license plate on the car that nearly hit one of the characters, the temperature today, a sale price in the carniceria: the number of the player who hit the home run in the bar the coterie just entered; the characters just cannot get away from the number 38.
A black cat goes out of its way to avoid crossing the coterie's path.
The thornbush in the park suddenly sprouts massive overgrowth and red flowers out of season.
A spider spins a cobweb completely covering the character's resting place in one day.
In the crowd flocking to or from a music festival three girls wearing fake flowers in their hair sing a song from the character's youth. Its lyrics may hold a message of prophecy.
The pattern of play in the chess games in the park eerily echoes the Primogens' maneuvers for power in the city.
The sodium lights in the parking lot flare up and flicker out in a specific, repeating rhythm.
Raccoons run amok in the alley behind a fried chicken joint, scattering the small bones in a very suggestive pattern.
A seagull drops a shoe with a human foot inside it onto the roof of Elysium.
A mass of ants crawl all over the place where the character was sitting, ignoring the rest of the bench.

A man with a jackhammer has three reflective yellow stripes on his jacket and seems to be across the street from the character, no matter where they are in the city. Other city worker jackets only have one yellow stripe.
A Roman denarius appears in the fountain after the character throws in a regular coin.
Everywhere the character looks at two windows, the one on the left always has the blind all the way down. The manifestation ends when they hear a gunshot.
An albino squirrel catches its foot in the grating over the subway nearest the character's haven.
The names on a wedding cake thrown in the dumpster behind an office building are the same as the names of the character and their former spouse.
A wasp's nest strongly resembles City Hall.
At midnight the cloud over the tallest skyscraper in the city looks like a man impaled on that building.

The King of Hearts (the "suicide king") keeps showing up: in a three-card monte game, the first card dealt in a poker game, embroidered on a gang banger's jacket, when a man named King commits suicide and it makes the headline crawl.
Everywhere the character goes, they see groups of pregnant women with baby carriages; one woman in particular wears a bright red scarf.
The dryers in the character's building begin spinning widdershins instead of clockwise.
Ask the player what shoes their character is wearing right now. They see the identical pair hanging over a power line. This happens for three nights in a row.
Three nights in a row the character hears a tour guide describe a murder to a crowd of tourists. The last time, the tour guide was speaking Chinese except for the murder description.
Three nights in a row, a different red SUV (a Lincoln Navigator) stops to mistakenly pick up the character in a rideshare mixup.
A rat runs across the character's path with a discarded heroin syringe stuck in its throat, then dies.
The character's haven casts no shadow in the full moon.
For one night, whenever the character sees a clock face or compass rose outdoors, they feel a strong urge to look into the direction of the wind.
Salt shakers near the character keep falling off tables or tipping over or being dropped by wait staff.
The keys to the characters' havens rust suddenly, and perhaps unnaturally quickly.
Wires, chains, cables, clotheslines, and the like in the characters' field of vision tend to hang in double loops, like handcuffs.
A sensationalistic YouTuber reports that a wolf at the zoo gave birth to a two-headed cub.
The weird colors in the night sky over the chemical plant match those in the aura of a stranger.
When viewed from the rooftop or on Google Maps, the pattern of street construction around the character's haven makes a large "N" (or a pair of "V's" or some other interesting symbol).
The character sees a magazine burning in a fire in a garbage drum; the cover model dresses like they do.
The pictures of local celebrities on the wall of the rib joint keep shifting their positions, or so it seems – the dust remains undisturbed.
Quotations and incidents from Macbeth recur coincidentally around the character, especially Lady Macbeth's line, "who would have thought the old man to have had so much blood in him."
The melting snow reveals a homeless man, frozen in the act of pointing toward the Prince's mansion.
A bike messenger wipes out against a van at the same instant that a bird flies into a glass window. Both van and window have the word "CLIFF" on them.
